elements.title: A distant brown dwarf coplanar to a warm Jupiter and a hot super-Earth (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
A distant brown dwarf coplanar to a warm Jupiter and a hot super-Earth

Analysis of long-term radial velocity data and transit time variations, induced by a super-Earth, a warm Jupiter and a brown dwarf in a coplanar orbit around the relatively young star TOI201.

  • Matías I. Jones
  • Luca Naponiello
  • Petr Kabath
Article17 Jun 2026

elements.title: Probing picometre-scale interlayer deformations via hyperbolic polaritons (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Probing picometre-scale interlayer deformations via hyperbolic polaritons

A new polaritonic optical method that uses the mid-infrared out-of-plane hyperbolic polaritons mode is described and experimentally validated to allow the examination of picometre-scale interlayer deformations, providing a bridge between nanomechanics and photonics.

  • Shu Zhang
  • Xiangdong Guo
  • Qing Dai
Article17 Jun 2026

elements.title: Optical fibre gripper for high-performance 3D micromanipulation (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Optical fibre gripper for high-performance 3D micromanipulation

A miniature three-dimensional optical fibre gripper enables powerful, precise micromanipulation of particles and single cells in confined spaces, bridging the gap between optical and mechanical tweezers.

  • Deng Pan
  • Kaiwen Liang
  • Dong Wu
Article17 Jun 2026

elements.title: A prototype differential atom interferometer for fundamental physics (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
A prototype differential atom interferometer for fundamental physics

A prototype differential atom interferometer operates at the standard quantum limit with no excess noise beyond atom shot noise, achieving performance in line with the specifications for future long-baseline atom interferometers.

  • C. F. A. Baynham
  • R. Hobson
  • M. G. D. van der Grinten
ArticleOpen Access17 Jun 2026

elements.title: Structure of the pre-initiation complex explains CMGE biogenesis (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Structure of the pre-initiation complex explains CMGE biogenesis

Cryo-electron microscopy and biochemical reconstitution experiments in yeast provide insight into the assembly of the CMGE complex, a helicase that establishes bidirectional DNA replication in eukaryotic cells, and elucidate the role of the firing factor Sld2.

  • Thomas Pühringer
  • Berta Canal
  • Alessandro Costa
ArticleOpen Access17 Jun 2026

elements.title: A 98-qubit trapped-ion quantum computer with all-to-all connectivity (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
A 98-qubit trapped-ion quantum computer with all-to-all connectivity

A new quantum computer, Quantinuum Helios, which is a 98-qubit trapped-ion quantum processor built on the QCCD architecture, demonstrates performance well beyond classical capabilities and provides a path for scaling up quantum computing.

  • Anthony Ransford
  • M. S. Allman
  • Justin G. Bohnet
ArticleOpen Access17 Jun 2026

elements.title: Fast formation to reinforce lithium-rich cathodes (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Fast formation to reinforce lithium-rich cathodes

Fast formation in lithium-ion batteries outperforms conventional slow formation, lowering costs and improving battery capacity, stability and cycle life, offering broader application to electrode systems.

  • Mengjian Fan
  • Jiantao Li
  • Qingshui Xie
Article17 Jun 2026

elements.title: Revealing competitive interfacial reactions in high-energy Li–S batteries (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Revealing competitive interfacial reactions in high-energy Li–S batteries

Visualization of concentration-driven phase segregation within high-concentration interfacial layers in the context of high-energy lithium–sulfur batteries using liquid-cell electrochemical transmission electron microscopy reveals competitive interfacial reactions under lean electrolyte conditions at different phase boundaries.

  • Shiyuan Zhou
  • Fei Pei
  • Hong-Gang Liao
Article17 Jun 2026

elements.title: Molecular basis of polyadenylated RNA fate determination in the nucleus (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Molecular basis of polyadenylated RNA fate determination in the nucleus

Biochemical, structural and cell biological analyses reveal that UAP56 (DDX39B) assembles with a TREX-2–like module that redirects non-functional polyadenylated RNAs from export to degradation.

  • Andrii Bugai
  • Ulrich Hohmann
  • Torben Heick Jensen
ArticleOpen Access17 Jun 2026

elements.title: Rock weathering can counteract river CO2 emissions induced by permafrost thaw (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Rock weathering can counteract river CO2 emissions induced by permafrost thaw

Permafrost thaw on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau increases rock-weathering rates while reducing river CO2 emissions, suggesting geological carbon fluxes may eventually outpace thaw-driven emissions.

  • Liwei Zhang
  • Aaron Bufe
  • Tom J. Battin
ArticleOpen Access17 Jun 2026

elements.title: Cortical development dynamics across autism spectrum disorder mouse models (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Cortical development dynamics across autism spectrum disorder mouse models

Using single-nucleus multi-omic sequencing, diverse autism spectrum disorder-linked gene mutations converge on transient, stage-specific disruptions in early brain development, and highlight sex-specific gene expression alterations.

  • Lena A. Schwarz
  • Christoph P. Dotter
  • Gaia Novarino
ArticleOpen Access17 Jun 2026

elements.title: A blastoporal organizer in a ctenophore (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
A blastoporal organizer in a ctenophore

Experiments using the comb jelly Mnemiopsis leidyi and the sea anemone Nematostella vectensis reveal that the emergence of a core signalling pathway may have been a key innovation enabling the transition to multicellularity in animals.

  • Stanislav Kremnyov
  • Tatiana Lebedeva
  • Andreas Hejnol
ArticleOpen Access17 Jun 2026

elements.title: Confined migration induces non-lethal DNA damage in developing neurons (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Confined migration induces non-lethal DNA damage in developing neurons

The migration of neurons in developing cerebral and cerebellar cortices is accompanied by massive DNA double-strand breaks due to mechanostress during passage through narrow interstitial spaces.

  • Zhejing Zhang
  • Andres Canela
  • Mineko Kengaku
ArticleOpen Access17 Jun 2026

elements.title: Analysis of 173,303 exomes and genomes in the Pakistan Genome Resource (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Analysis of 173,303 exomes and genomes in the Pakistan Genome Resource

The Pakistan Genome Resource compiles biobank data from 173,303 individuals with high familial relatedness, broadening the catalogue of human genetic variation and establishing a population-specific genomic reference for Pakistan.

  • Christopher Koch
  • Shareef Khalid
  • Danish Saleheen
ArticleOpen Access17 Jun 2026

elements.title: A mosaic of whole-body representations on the human precentral gyrus (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
A mosaic of whole-body representations on the human precentral gyrus

A comprehensive map of the human motor cortex at single-neuron resolution is described.

  • Darrel R. Deo
  • Elizaveta V. Okorokova
  • Francis R. Willett
ArticleOpen Access17 Jun 2026

elements.title: Spatial distribution of the proteome in the human body and in cancers (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Spatial distribution of the proteome in the human body and in cancers

A spatially resolved map of the human proteome across a variety of healthy tissues and cancers provides wide-ranging insights in developmental biology and oncology, and could aid the identification of therapeutic targets and development of treatments for cancer.

  • Liang Yue
  • Wenhao Jiang
  • Tiannan Guo
ArticleOpen Access17 Jun 2026

elements.title: Lethal plague outbreaks in Lake Baikal hunter-gatherers 5,500 years ago (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Lethal plague outbreaks in Lake Baikal hunter-gatherers 5,500 years ago

Analyses of ancient DNA from hunter-gatherers near Lake Baikal in southeast Siberia around 5,500 years ago indicate that highly virulent Yersinia pestis emerged earlier than previously estimated, far from the next known cases of infection in Late Neolithic Europe.

  • Ruairidh Macleod
  • Frederik V. Seersholm
  • Eske Willerslev
ArticleOpen Access17 Jun 2026

elements.title: Mapping the neuronal building blocks of human language with language models (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Mapping the neuronal building blocks of human language with language models

Wide-scale recordings reveal neurons in the human brain that encode fundamental components of language such as the grammatical relationships between words, their parts of speech and the higher-order syntactic structure of phrases and sentences.

  • Jing Cai
  • Yoav Kfir
  • Ziv M. Williams
ArticleOpen Access17 Jun 2026

elements.title: Towards autonomous medical artificial intelligence agents (Nature - research articles)
elements.contents:
Towards autonomous medical artificial intelligence agents

A large language model artificial intelligence agent operating in a sandboxed electronic health record system can autonomously take patient histories, order tests, interpret findings, diagnose conditions and propose treatments, outperforming experienced clinicians while adhering to safety standards and clinical guidelines.

  • Dyke Ferber
  • Lars Hilgers
  • Jakob Nikolas Kather
ArticleOpen Access17 Jun 2026
